walkthroughs.body_html:
Decision Making to Improve Operational Performance — a core area of A-Level Business Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Decision Making to Improve Operational Performance brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Decision Making to Improve Operational Performance.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Modigliani and Miller's irrelevance theorem was published in:

options: Annual cost calculation
Cost of capital
Capital ceiling
Credit cycle

mcqs.q: What is a brand in marketing?
options: A brand is just the logo on a product.
A combination of name, design, symbols and associations that distinguishes a product and creates customer perception and loyalty — more than just a logo.
A brand is the company that makes a product.
Just-in-time means finishing work right before the deadline.

The external macro-environment: Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal and Environmental factors affecting a business.
PESTLE stands for Profit, Earnings, Sales, Trade, Loans, Equity.
PESTLE analyses the internal strengths and weaknesses of a business.
PESTLE stands for Profit, Earnings, Sales, Trade, Loans, Equity.
Just-in-time means delivering products to customers exactly on time.
Holding minimal stock and receiving inputs only when needed for production — reducing storage costs but increasing vulnerability to supply disruption.
Just-in-time means finishing work right before the deadline.
